question: Which action shows proper infection control when collecting a specimen?

options.A: Recapping used needles using both hands to prevent spills
options.B: Using clean gloves and performing hand hygiene before and after
options.C: Wiping the specimen container exterior with bare hands
options.D: Storing open specimen tubes on the patient's bed sheets

explanation: Hand hygiene and gloves protect both you and your patient from spreading germs. Always clean your hands and glove up!

question: What is the maximum recommended time for a single suction pass?

options.A: 3 to 5 minutes
options.B: 1 to 2 minutes
options.C: 30 to 45 seconds
options.D: 10 to 15 seconds

explanation: Limiting passes to 10 to 15 seconds prevents the patient from running out of oxygen and developing dangerous heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which group of vitamins is known as fat-soluble?

options.A: Vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.B: Vitamin C and the B-complex group
options.C: Calcium, iron, and potassium
options.D: Amino acids and plant extracts

explanation: Think of vitamins A, D, E, and K as the ones that dissolve in fat and can hang out in our body's fatty tissues and liver for later use.

question: What crucial warning must you give a patient who takes daily anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Only take the pills on days when you feel a headache coming on
options.B: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without consulting your doctor
options.C: Stop the medication immediately if you go one week without a seizure
options.D: Take a double dose whenever you feel stressed or tired

explanation: Spot on! Quitting anti-seizure meds abruptly can trigger dangerous rebound seizures or status epilepticus. Always taper safely with a doctor's guidance.

question: During a home visit to an 80-year-old client, what safety check should the nurse prioritize to prevent common injuries?

options.A: Removing all chairs from the house to encourage standing
options.B: Testing the patient's ability to run a half-marathon outdoors
options.C: Checking if the patient can drive a heavy transport vehicle
options.D: Inspecting floors for loose rugs and poor lighting to stop falls

explanation: Fall prevention is a critical part of geriatric care, and checking home hazards directly prevents injuries. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which test is commonly used to screen for too much adrenaline breakdown in a suspected pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Morning serum cortisol levels
options.B: Serum fasting blood glucose
options.C: 24-hour urinary metanephrines
options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

explanation: Collecting urine over 24 hours lets us measure metanephrines, which are the leftover waste products of extra adrenaline and noradrenaline over a full day.

question: What form of the malaria parasite does a mosquito first inject into a person?

options.A: Merozoites
options.B: Gametocytes
options.C: Zygotes
options.D: Sporozoites

explanation: Correct! Infected mosquitoes carry sporozoites in their salivary glands and inject them right into your skin and blood when they bite.

question: Which of these statements is true when it comes to asking a patient directly about suicide?

options.A: Asking directly opens the door for help and does not cause suicidal thoughts
options.B: Nurses should only ask about suicide if the patient brings it up first
options.C: Asking about suicide will plant the idea into a healthy patient's mind
options.D: Direct questioning is discouraged because it increases patient agitation

explanation: Brilliant! Asking directly doesn't put the idea in their head—it actually brings immense relief because it shows you care and understand how much pain they are in.

question: Which Nigerian agency leads the fight against drug trafficking and abuse?

options.A: Frsc
options.B: Nafdac
options.C: Nysc
options.D: NDLEA

explanation: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) is the main body responsible for tackling illicit drug crimes in Nigeria.

question: How can a nurse best support a patient who is going through physical rehabilitation on the ward?

options.A: Limit fluid intake to reduce the need for assisted bathroom trips
options.B: Discourage physical movement until formal therapy sessions resume
options.C: Encourage the patient to perform tasks independently using learned adaptive methods
options.D: Complete all personal care tasks for the patient to save time and prevent fatigue

explanation: We want to empower them! Letting patients practice their skills during routine care builds their confidence and strength. Keep up the great clinical mindset!

question: As a student nurse, what should be your main focus when giving nutrition advice to a patient?

options.A: Diagnosing eating disorders
options.B: Helping patients make healthy food choices
options.C: Calculating daily calorie intake
options.D: Prescribing strict medical diets

explanation: Great job thinking like a nurse! Nutrition counselling isn't about rigid rules; it's about guiding people toward healthy, sustainable food decisions that fit their everyday lives.

question: When does a nurse use the number 703 in a BMI calculation?

options.A: When adjusting for athletes with high muscle mass
options.B: When the patient's measurements are in pounds and inches
options.C: When the patient is measured in kilograms and meters
options.D: When calculating BMI for an elderly patient

explanation: The number 703 is a handy conversion factor used to balance out imperial units (pounds and inches). Simple as that!

question: A patient has a stubborn rash that won't go away with standard treatment, so a skin biopsy is ordered. What is the goal?

options.A: Confirm a definitive diagnosis and guide treatment
options.B: Decontaminate the skin surface from bacterial flora
options.C: Remove all inflamed nerve endings causing itching
options.D: Prevent the rash from spreading to other body parts

explanation: When standard creams don't work, a biopsy helps pin down the exact problem so the healthcare team can choose the right medicine that actually works.

question: Why do we need to eat water-soluble vitamins more often than fat-soluble ones?

options.A: They cannot be absorbed without large amounts of dietary fat.
options.B: They are destroyed instantly by stomach acid during digestion.
options.C: The liver stores them in massive quantities that deplete rapidly.
options.D: Excess amounts are quickly flushed out of the body in the urine.

explanation: Exactly! Because they dissolve in water, your kidneys easily wash away any daily extra. That's why a steady daily supply from your diet is key.

question: Which food group is the body's main and quickest source of energy?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Fats
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs break down quickly into glucose, which acts as the favorite fuel for your cells and brain.

question: Why should you do a quick physical assessment right after the steam session ends?

options.A: To check if the bed linens need washing
options.B: To evaluate how well the treatment worked
options.C: To see if the patient needs a snack or drink
options.D: To make sure the electrical cord is cool

explanation: Spot on! Comparing your notes now with your baseline check tells you if the therapy did its job.

question: What must the pelvic floor muscles do to allow someone to pass urine?

options.A: Relax
options.B: Vibrate rapidly
options.C: Rotate outward
options.D: Contract tightly

explanation: That's right! To pee freely, these muscles have to let go and relax so the path is open.

question: Why is educating community and religious leaders an effective way to fight child trafficking?

options.A: They possess the legal power to arrest and prosecute criminals
options.B: They provide free medical treatment to all trafficking victims
options.C: They fund all government anti-trafficking agencies
options.D: They can help monitor for suspicious strangers and false agents

explanation: Local leaders know everyone in their area and can easily spot outsiders trying to prey on vulnerable children.

question: Why is a tension pneumothorax such a major emergency?

options.A: Trapped air builds up pressure and shifts the heart and major blood vessels
options.B: It stops the kidneys from producing urine within minutes
options.C: It floods both lungs with thick, yellow mucus
options.D: It causes an immediate massive infection in the bronchial tubes

explanation: Correct! Trapped air keeps stacking up like a balloon, pushing everything in the chest sideways and stopping blood from returning to the heart.

question: A mother brings her healthy 14-week-old infant to the primary health clinic. Which group of vaccines is due for this visit?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.B: Measles first dose and Yellow Fever vaccine
options.C: Rotavirus first dose and Pentavalent first dose
options.D: Pentavalent third dose, OPV 3, IPV, and PCV 3

explanation: At 14 weeks, infants receive the third doses of Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV, along with the first dose of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: What is the primary benefit of using a blameless incident reporting system in a hospital?

options.A: It eliminates all documentation requirements for nurses
options.B: It reduces the cost of purchasing medical insurance
options.C: It ensures that negligent workers are quickly dismissed
options.D: It encourages staff to report errors so system flaws can be fixed

explanation: Blameless reporting focuses on correcting root system problems rather than punishing workers, which encourages honest reporting of mistakes. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the key feature of a latent tuberculosis infection?

options.A: The patient has a productive cough and bloody sputum
options.B: The person is asymptomatic and cannot spread the disease
options.C: The bacteria are rapidly multiplying throughout the bloodstream
options.D: Chest X-rays consistently show severe lung cavity destruction

explanation: Latent TB means the germs are sleeping safely inside the body, kept in check by your immune system. The person feels fine and cannot pass it to others.

question: A hospital quality team wants to know the exact percentage of patients discharged in under four days. Which graph helps find this easiest?

options.A: An ogive
options.B: A stem-and-leaf plot
options.C: A scatter plot
options.D: A pie chart

explanation: Spot on! Ogives shine when we need to find running portions and percentages below or above a specific time frame.

question: What do we call the mismatch when a baby's head is too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.A: Uterine inertia
options.B: Secondary power failure
options.C: Occipitoposterior arrest
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Spot on! Cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) simply means the baby's head size or the pelvis shape makes a normal vaginal delivery impossible.

question: What are the three parts of the small intestine in order, starting right after the stomach?

options.A: Duodenum, ileum, cecum
options.B: Jejunum, ileum, duodenum
options.C: Duodenum, jejunum, ileum
options.D: Ileum, duodenum, jejunum

explanation: Easy to remember once you say it a few times: food flows from the stomach into the duodenum, then the jejunum, and finally the ileum!

question: Why do nurses and doctors use a standard classification system for FGM?

options.A: To help healthcare workers document and assess clinical needs
options.B: To assign legal penalties to specific practitioners
options.C: To determine the correct surgical reversal technique
options.D: To calculate the financial cost of hospital treatment

explanation: Exactly! Knowing the specific type helps nurses understand the patient's history and plan the best, most sensitive care possible.

question: What is the main purpose of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) sticker on a vaccine bottle?

options.A: To signal when the needle has been contaminated by bacteria
options.B: To show if the vial has been exposed to cumulative heat that could ruin its potency
options.C: To indicate the exact manufacturing date and batch number of the product
options.D: To measure the remaining volume of liquid inside the glass vial

explanation: The VVM is a nurse's best friend! It changes color when the vaccine has seen too much heat, letting you know instantly if it's still safe to use.

question: Why is the nurse's voice so important in a collaborative healthcare team?

options.A: Nurses hold sole legal authority over all hospital budget allocations
options.B: Nurses are the only professionals trained to diagnose chronic illnesses
options.C: Nurses dictate the operational hours of every hospital department
options.D: Nurses spend the most time at the bedside observing patients

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses are right there at the bedside day and night, they spot subtle changes in patients before anyone else does.

question: Which body receptor is mainly responsible for the pain-relieving power of strong opioids?

options.A: Alpha receptor
options.B: Mu receptor
options.C: Beta receptor
options.D: Gamma receptor

explanation: The mu receptor is the main target for opioids to kill pain, though it's also why strong opioids can cause drowsiness and slow breathing.

question: Which parts of the body usually show signs of vitamin or nutrient shortages first?

options.A: Parts with fast-growing cells like skin, hair, and nails
options.B: Major blood vessels and heart valves
options.C: Hard tissues like bones and deep skeletal muscles
options.D: Internal organs like the liver and kidneys

explanation: Because skin, hair, and nails replace their cells so quickly, they show signs of trouble way before deeper tissues do.

question: What is the main fertility option for a patient who has no fallopian tubes at all?

options.A: Tubal reanastomosis surgery
options.B: In vitro fertilization (IVF)
options.C: Endometrial ablation therapy
options.D: Ovarian hormone stimulation alone

explanation: Spot on! Since IVF places a fertilized egg directly into the uterus, it completely bypasses the need for fallopian tubes.

question: Why is educating parents about their child's chronic condition so important?

options.A: It prevents the child from ever growing up
options.B: It turns parents into licensed medical doctors
options.C: It empowers them to provide safe daily care and advocate for their child
options.D: It ensures the parents never need to visit a clinic again

explanation: Well-informed parents can manage home routines effectively and speak up for their child's needs in healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: Two nurses have totally different working styles, which causes minor daily friction between them. How is the best way to view this?

options.A: One of the nurses must be fired immediately for misconduct
options.B: It is a normal interpersonal clash of styles rather than a moral failure
options.C: The hospital building design is entirely to blame for their frustration
options.D: They will eventually agree on everything if left alone long enough

explanation: People naturally work differently—some are fast-paced, others meticulous. Recognizing this as a simple style difference helps teams manage tension without making it personal.

question: Which tool is commonly used by nurses to check a patient's risk of developing pressure sores upon admission?

options.A: Apgar Score
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Braden Scale
options.D: Pain Numeric Rating Scale

explanation: The Braden Scale is your go-to clinical tool! It checks things like moisture, mobility, and nutrition to give you a clear score of a patient's pressure sore risk. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the key difference between a synthetic drug and a semi-synthetic drug?

options.A: Synthetic drugs only come from plant roots, while semi-synthetic drugs come exclusively from mineral rocks.
options.B: Semi-synthetic medications require no clinical trials, whereas fully synthetic medications require extensive testing.
options.C: Synthetic drugs cannot be given orally, whereas semi-synthetic drugs can only be given via intravenous injection.
options.D: Semi-synthetic drugs modify a natural base compound in a lab, while synthetic drugs are built entirely from scratch.

explanation: Think of semi-synthetic drugs as natural molecules upgraded in a lab, while purely synthetic ones are built from scratch using basic chemicals.

question: Why would a researcher choose to observe heavy drinkers instead of forcing an experiment where people drink alcohol for years?

options.A: Alcohol abuse is too rare to study in a clinical trial setting
options.B: Experimental trials cannot use statistical analysis
options.C: Observational studies are much more expensive to conduct
options.D: It is unethical to force participants to consume alcohol for an experiment

explanation: Well reasoned! We can never intentionally put people in harm's way or force them to take harmful substances just for an experiment. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why do traditional beliefs often blame ancestral displeasure for psychological distress?

options.A: To show that physical injuries cause all brain disorders
options.B: To discourage individuals from talking to their neighbors
options.C: To prove that modern science has all the correct answers
options.D: To encourage people to maintain family traditions and moral codes

explanation: Makes total sense! Attributing illness to broken taboos or ancestral anger reinforces community morality and the importance of heritage.

question: A client comes to you asking for advice on diet and irregular ovulation. What is the best starting point?

options.A: Focus on whole foods, healthy weight management, and essential micronutrients
options.B: Rely entirely on heavy vitamin supplements instead of eating meals
options.C: Drink large amounts of caffeinated coffee to boost resting metabolism
options.D: Eliminate all carbohydrates completely from your daily meals

explanation: Awesome choice! Real, wholesome food and steady weight management give the body the stable foundation it needs for natural hormonal balance.

question: Why is postpartum hemorrhage a huge risk after a mother delivers twins?

options.A: The overstretched uterus contracts poorly after birth.
options.B: The placenta is always retained inside the fallopian tubes.
options.C: The mother has too much iron in her bloodstream.
options.D: Blood clotting factors completely disappear during labor.

explanation: Brilliant reasoning! Carrying multiples stretches the uterine muscles a lot. Afterward, it sometimes struggles to clamp back down firmly (we call this uterine atony), making bleeding a major risk to watch for.

question: A community nurse is teaching rural farmers how to avoid hookworm. What is the best practical advice to share?

options.A: Wear protective footwear consistently when working outdoors
options.B: Avoid eating raw vegetables harvested from flooded river valleys
options.C: Take prophylactic antibiotics every morning before breakfast
options.D: Boil all drinking water for at least two hours before consumption

explanation: Since hookworm larvae wait in the soil to burrow through bare skin, putting on footwear is a simple, life-saving habit for farmers.

question: What does Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) ask organizations to look at?

options.A: Strict compliance with advertising laws alone
options.B: Social, environmental, and economic impacts of operations
options.C: Only the immediate quarterly financial profits
options.D: The personal religious beliefs of every employee

explanation: CSR means a healthcare facility or company cares about more than just making money—they also look after their community and the environment.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four key elements needed to prove malpractice?

options.A: Guilt
options.B: Damages
options.C: Duty
options.D: Breach

explanation: To prove malpractice, you need duty, breach, causation, and damages. 'Guilt' belongs in criminal law, not civil malpractice cases.

question: Where are the receptors for water-soluble hormones located?

options.A: Inside the mitochondrial matrix
options.B: On the outer cell surface
options.C: Floating freely in blood plasma
options.D: Inside the cell nucleus

question: How can bad or missing documentation put a patient in danger?

options.A: It automatically increases the patient's hospital bill
options.B: It can lead to missed interventions and errors
options.C: It causes delays in hospital discharge procedures
options.D: It prevents doctors from writing new prescriptions

explanation: Spot on! If care details are missing, the next nurse might repeat a treatment or miss a dangerous change in the patient's condition.

question: Why is just counting calories often not enough when caring for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Calories change drastically depending on the time of day a meal is served
options.B: Calories do not reflect whether the body can actually absorb and use the nutrients
options.C: Patient metabolism makes calorie tracking completely impossible in a hospital
options.D: Processed foods always have lower calorie counts than raw food items

explanation: Great thinking! A meal can be packed with calories yet lack the vital building blocks our cells and tissues need to heal.

question: Where do ectopic pregnancies most frequently happen?

options.A: The endocervical canal
options.B: The abdominal cavity
options.C: The urinary bladder
options.D: The fallopian tube

explanation: Correct! Most ectopic pregnancies get stuck in the fallopian tube because the embryo implants on its way down to the uterus. Excellent clinical recall!

question: What is the main feature of an urban 'food desert'?

options.A: Excessive government control over neighborhood food prices
options.B: A complete absence of any stores selling edible products
options.C: An abundance of local farms producing fresh vegetables
options.D: A lack of nearby supermarkets offering fresh, affordable food

explanation: A food desert is an area where fresh, healthy food is hard to find, leaving people relying mostly on processed snacks from corner shops.

question: Which group in the community is usually hit hardest by nutritional food taboos?

options.A: Young adult working males
options.B: Pregnant and lactating women
options.C: Unmarried teenage boys
options.D: Elderly male community leaders

explanation: Expectant and breastfeeding mothers need extra nutrition, which unfortunately makes them prime targets for restrictive cultural rules.

question: Why are babies born to mothers with severe placental issues often smaller than expected for their gestational age?

options.A: The umbilical cord absorbs most of the nutrients before they reach the fetus.
options.B: Amniotic fluid volume increases and crowds out the growing baby.
options.C: The placenta cannot supply adequate oxygen and nutrients for normal fetal growth.
options.D: The mother restricts her food intake out of fear of complications.

question: Why is ophthalmoscopy useful for monitoring chronic systemic diseases like diabetes?

options.A: It directly measures the current level of sugar floating in the blood

options.C: It tracks how well the kidneys are filtering waste from the body
options.D: It calculates the total amount of protein stored in body tissues

explanation: Systemic diseases like diabetes damage small blood vessels throughout the body, and the tiny vessels in the retina can be directly observed during this exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do nurses use a pH testing strip when checking a newly placed nasogastric tube?

options.A: To test how acidic the fluid pulled from the tube is
options.B: To check the expiry date of the food formula
options.C: To check if the patient has a stomach ulcer
options.D: To measure the sugar level in the feed

explanation: Stomach acid is very sour! Testing the pH of fluid from the tube helps us confirm the tip is safely inside the acidic stomach, not the lungs.

question: How does metabolic stress differ from simple starvation?

options.A: Metabolic stress lowers the heart rate to save body nutrients.
options.B: Metabolic stress forces high energy use while blocking normal tissue conservation.
options.C: Simple starvation causes sudden swelling all over the body.
options.D: Simple starvation causes a faster breakdown of muscle than major trauma.

explanation: While simple starvation triggers energy-saving mechanisms, inflammatory metabolic stress forces continuous tissue breakdown without letting the body conserve resources. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h3)

question: A community nurse notices three children from the same street presenting with high fever and yellow eyes. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Advise the parents to keep the children away from school without notifying anyone
options.B: Report the suspected cases according to local surveillance guidelines and investigate further
options.C: Assume it is a normal seasonal illness and provide standard rest advice at home
options.D: Wait until next month to see if more children in the neighborhood get sick

explanation: Spotting a cluster of serious symptoms requires prompt reporting and investigation to prevent a wider outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Providing emergency surgery for severe trauma victims
options.B: Managing end-stage organ failure with palliative care
options.C: Early detection and prompt intervention for mild problems
options.D: Preventing a disease from ever occurring in a healthy person

explanation: Secondary prevention catches conditions early when they are easiest to treat and manage successfully. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h7)

question: What is the most important instruction for a patient after an IVP procedure is finished?

options.A: Take a strong diuretic medication to stimulate urine flow
options.B: Avoid eating any solid foods until the following morning
options.C: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush out the contrast dye
options.D: Remain completely on bed rest for the next twenty-four hours

explanation: Water is the best helper here! Drinking plenty of fluids helps the kidneys wash the remaining contrast dye safely out of the body.

question: Which cells are the main ones responsible for humoral immunity?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Cytotoxic T cells
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: B cells

explanation: B cells are the masters of humoral immunity! They mature into plasma cells that pump out circulating antibodies into your body fluids.

question: How should a nurse best approach diet education for a patient going home with a new health condition?

options.A: Assume they already know basics from TV
options.B: Focus only on foods they cannot eat
options.C: Tailor teaching to their lifestyle and culture
options.D: Hand out a complex medical textbook to read

explanation: You got it! Teaching works best when it fits the patient's daily life, culture, and personal background.

question: Why must you know the anatomy of the vulva well before taking a sample?

options.A: To determine the exact hormonal cycle day of the patient accurately

options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling any discomfort during the procedure

question: Why should hospitals offer counseling and support to nurses involved in errors?

options.B: To prevent them from talking to hospital management ever again
options.C: To ensure they can be easily monitored for future illegal activities
options.D: To replace their clinical training with psychological theory

explanation: Clinical errors take a heavy emotional toll. Providing support helps nurses heal and protects them from burning out.

question: What is the primary purpose of communication in community health nursing?

options.A: Completing hospital discharge paperwork quickly
options.B: Diagnosing rare surgical complications independently
options.C: Enforcing strict rules in the neighborhood clinic
options.D: Building trust and delivering health education

explanation: Community nurses use communication primarily to build relationships, gain trust, and teach people how to care for their health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: What triggers the sudden rush of milk right after childbirth?

options.A: An immediate rise in maternal body temperature
options.B: The sudden drop in estrogen and progesterone levels
options.C: The total disappearance of prolactin from the blood
options.D: A massive spike in placental hormone production

explanation: Exactly! Once the placenta is delivered, those blocking hormones plummet, allowing prolactin to finally do its job and bring in the milk.

question: Which of these is a direct cost when buying medicines?

options.A: Monthly electricity bills for the pharmacy store
options.B: The invoice price paid to the drug manufacturer
options.C: Printing costs for general hospital stationery
options.D: Salaries paid to the hospital security guards
