question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to care for skin receiving radiation therapy?

options.A: Scrub the treatment area firmly with a washcloth daily
options.B: Use heating pads on the skin to relieve soreness
options.C: Wash the area gently with mild soap and warm water
options.D: Apply strong perfumed lotions right before treatment

explanation: Treated skin is extra fragile. Gentle cleansing with mild soap and water protects the delicate skin barrier. You're mastering patient care!

question: Why do incubatory carriers give nurses headaches when trying to stop the spread of disease?

options.A: They spread pathogens before anyone realizes they are sick
options.B: They only transmit infections through contaminated drinking water
options.C: They carry drug-resistant bacteria that resist all antibiotics
options.D: They refuse to take their prescribed medications in the ward

explanation: Since they look and feel healthy right now, nobody suspects they are passing germs around until symptoms finally show up later.

question: Why do some women still seek out traditional practitioners for gishiri cuts instead of going to a hospital?

options.A: Government policy requires trying traditional methods first
options.B: Hospitals mandate the procedure for all pregnant women
options.C: Traditional healers offer free antibiotics and modern anesthesia
options.D: Cultural beliefs strongly link reproductive issues to a traditional diagnosis

explanation: Deeply ingrained cultural norms and traditional explanations for illnesses drive patients toward local healers before or instead of formal health facilities. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which health condition can significantly delay the normal wound healing process?

options.A: Primary hypertension
options.B: Acute tension headache
options.C: Uncontrolled diabetes
options.D: Mild seasonal allergies

explanation: High blood sugar impairs circulation and white blood cell function, which slows down tissue repair and delays safe suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is a major reason why Nigeria is facing a shortage of skilled nurses right now?

options.A: A complete ban on private nursing practice
options.B: The mass migration of healthcare professionals abroad
options.C: Mandatory retirement at age thirty
options.D: The total closure of all nursing training institutions

explanation: Spot on. Many skilled nurses are travelling abroad for better opportunities, leaving a big gap at home.

question: How is custodial care traditionally provided in most Nigerian communities?

options.A: Exclusively through government-funded nursing homes
options.B: By international insurance companies paying for home aides
options.C: Through mandatory hospital stays for all elderly citizens
options.D: Through extended family networks and shared family duty

explanation: Nigerian culture traditionally relies on the extended family system to care for aging or disabled relatives at home. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why is transparency critical when mobilising a community for health action?

options.A: It stops villagers from asking questions about disease names
options.B: It guarantees that the federal government will send more funds
options.C: It builds lasting trust between the health team and the public
options.D: It prevents nurses from working long hours at the clinic

explanation: Open communication about goals, resources, and challenges removes suspicion and encourages people to cooperate fully. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h2)

question: A surgical ward notices their wound infection rates jumping up and down wildly every month. What does this suggest?

options.A: The ward has inconsistent infection control practices that put patients at risk
options.B: The nursing staff is following standardized protocols too rigidly
options.C: The laboratory is simply mislabelling routine blood cultures
options.D: The hospital is experiencing normal, safe biological variation in healing

explanation: Well reasoned! Wildly swinging infection rates mean infection control isn't being done the same way every time, putting patients in danger.

question: What administrative problem frequently disrupts the availability of essential medicines in clinics?

options.A: Too many pharmaceutical factories opening up in local towns
options.B: An excessive surplus of trained doctors in rural areas
options.C: Patients refusing to visit health facilities during dry seasons
options.D: Poor supply chain management and distribution bottlenecks

explanation: Even when drugs are budgeted for, weak logistics and transport systems often prevent them from reaching remote clinics on time. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why are run charts and graphs so commonly used in healthcare data analysis?

options.A: To replace patient medical records with colorful artwork
options.B: To hide negative patient statistics from regulatory inspectors
options.C: To calculate the daily nursing staff roster automatically
options.D: To help clinical teams easily visualize trends and patterns over time

explanation: Graphs make it super easy to look at numbers and instantly see if things are getting better or worse over weeks and months.

question: What does it mean when a patient's emotional distress is described as 'somaticized'?

options.A: Seeking immediate help from a specialized psychiatrist
options.B: Denying that any mental or physical health problem exists
options.C: Isolating oneself from family and friends during a crisis
options.D: Expressing emotional pain entirely through physical bodily complaints

explanation: Think of somaticization as the body speaking what the heart cannot. It's when emotional pain turns into very real physical signs like headaches, stomach aches, or crushing fatigue.

question: Why is splitting funds across federal, state, and local governments a big problem in Nigeria's health system?

options.A: It prevents international donors from sending any financial aid
options.B: It makes tracking spending and resource distribution difficult
options.C: It forces all private hospitals to close down immediately
options.D: It automatically increases out-of-pocket payments by fifty percent

explanation: When money comes from many uncoordinated sources, it becomes tough to manage efficiently or ensure it actually reaches grassroots clinics. Spotting these system gaps is key for a brilliant nurse!

question: What should you do immediately if you find an expired drug in the crash cart during a check?

options.A: Report and replace it right away
options.B: Leave it until the end of the week
options.C: Use it on the next stable patient
options.D: Hide it in the bottom drawer

explanation: You got it! Expired drugs can fail when you need them most, so swapping them out instantly keeps our patients safe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is community profiling necessary before launching a health project?

options.A: It prevents outsiders from visiting the community
options.B: It automatically cures local malnutrition cases
options.C: It proves to the government that nurses are working hard
options.D: It reveals the unique demographics and culture of the area

explanation: Profiling gives health workers clear baseline data about who lives there and how they live, guiding appropriate planning. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why must nurses work to eliminate personal bias regarding gender roles in the clinic?

options.A: Hospital management requires all nurses to pass a gender exam
options.B: Biases prevent nurses from dispensing medications properly
options.C: Ministry of health guidelines ban nurses from talking to men
options.D: Biased attitudes can make men feel unwelcome and drive them away from care

explanation: When nurses act judgmentally or ignore fathers, it reinforces the belief that health clinics are not meant for men. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: Where is the best place inside a vaccine fridge to store sensitive vaccines?

options.A: On the middle shelves
options.B: Packed tight against the cooling coils
options.C: In the door storage bins
options.D: Directly on the floor panel

explanation: The middle shelves keep the most even temperature. Doors and floor areas get too many temperature swings, which can ruin the vaccines.

question: A family member has newly diagnosed hypertension and requires a low-salt diet. What is the most practical nursing advice for the household cook?

options.A: Prepare two completely different meals every single day for every person
options.B: Stop cooking altogether and buy canned processed foods for everyone
options.C: Add extra salt to the main pot and give the patient plain water
options.D: Cook the base meal with minimal salt and let others add salt at the table

explanation: This approach keeps cooking manageable for the household while protecting the health of the family member with hypertension. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h6)

question: Why is immunization considered a fundamental component of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It is delivered exclusively inside major tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: It replaces the need for proper sanitation and clean drinking water
options.C: It provides affordable, community-based disease prevention for all
options.D: It focuses on treating advanced stages of communicable diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care aims to bring essential health services as close as possible to where people live, making preventive measures like vaccines easily accessible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: A patient comes in with yellow eyes (sclera) and dark urine. What process is likely happening?

options.A: Sudden increase in blood clotting factors causing blockages
options.B: Dangerous drop in white blood cells leading to severe infection
options.C: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells releasing bilirubin
options.D: Severe lack of dietary iron causing spoon-shaped nails

explanation: Yellowing eyes and skin point to hemolysis—where red blood cells break down too fast, releasing excess bilirubin into the body.

question: What is antimicrobial resistance?

options.A: Bacteria mutating to grow larger in size under drug treatment
options.B: Microbes surviving exposure to drugs that previously destroyed them
options.C: The human immune system rejecting prescribed pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Patients developing allergies to common antibiotics over time

explanation: Antimicrobial resistance occurs when pathogens adapt and survive treatments that used to kill them effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h1)

question: What is an important duty of a community health nurse when dealing with voluntary agencies?

options.A: Referring vulnerable patients to appropriate agency programs
options.B: Managing the global headquarters of faith-based charities
options.C: Auditing the financial tax accounts of all international donors
options.D: Passing new national legislation for non-profit groups

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, knowing what local agencies offer helps you connect your patients to free or low-cost support outside the hospital.

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a clinical audit in a reproductive health unit?

options.A: To increase the amount of financial profit the hospital makes
options.B: To find staff members to fire after an adverse event happens
options.C: To compare actual patient outcomes and care against established standards
options.D: To reduce the number of medical records kept in the filing room

explanation: Correct! Clinical audits help us look at our current care practices, spot gaps, and find ways to improve our nursing service.

question: Why is pulling your mask down around your neck during a break a bad idea?

options.A: It violates fashion codes
options.B: It stretches out the elastic bands forever
options.C: It contaminates the clean inside of your mask with germs from your neck skin
options.D: It blocks blood flow to your head

explanation: Pulling it to your neck exposes the inner lining to skin oils and germs, which you then breathe right back in!

question: Why is tiopronin often preferred over D-penicillamine in modern practice?

options.A: It generally presents a better and more tolerable side effect profile
options.B: It completely cures the genetic mutation responsible for the condition
options.C: It can be taken just once a year as a slow-release subcutaneous depot
options.D: It works by dissolving calcium oxalate stones instead of cystine

explanation: Tiopronin is much kinder to the patient's body! It causes fewer severe allergic and autoimmune reactions than D-penicillamine, helping patients stick to their treatment.

question: What does 'precision' measure in an information retrieval search?

options.A: The percentage of articles written by registered nurses
options.B: The proportion of retrieved documents that are actually relevant
options.C: The total number of seconds the computer takes to search
options.D: The exact number of spelling errors found in the abstract

explanation: Precision evaluates how well your search weeded out useless results, telling you what percentage of what you found was truly useful. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)

question: What are the tiny, finger-like folds inside the small intestine that soak up all our nutrients called?

options.A: Villi
options.B: Sphincters
options.C: Haustra
options.D: Rugae

explanation: Brilliant! Villi (and their even tinier microvilli) create a massive surface area inside your small intestine so your body can absorb as many nutrients as possible.

question: Why are driving restrictions commonly given to individuals recently diagnosed with epilepsy?

options.A: To protect the patient and public from sudden loss of consciousness behind the wheel
options.B: To encourage patients to use public transport for their routine blood tests
options.C: To prevent the car engine from triggering abnormal brain wave activity
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing vehicle insurance

explanation: It's all about safety! Because seizures can happen without warning, blacking out while driving puts both the driver and innocent pedestrians at severe risk.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient from a remote mountainous region with high rates of goiter. What public health program should the nurse support?

options.A: Teaching deep-sea fishing techniques
options.B: Introducing desert camel farming
options.C: Building large industrial rice mills
options.D: Promoting universal salt iodization programs

explanation: Mountain areas often lack iodine in their local soil and food, making iodized salt the best and easiest way to protect community health.

question: Which tool helps a patient who struggles to bend down to wash their lower legs and feet?

options.A: A long-handled sponge
options.B: A mechanical hoist
options.C: A standard walking frame
options.D: A raised toilet seat

explanation: Brilliant! A long-handled sponge is a simple yet clever device that lets patients reach their feet easily without straining their backs.

question: Why should nurses avoid heavy medical jargon when talking to community members?

options.A: Using simple words makes the nurse appear less educated to patients
options.B: Jargon automatically cures diseases faster than simple language
options.C: Patients may become confused and fail to understand the required health action
options.D: Medical terms are illegal to use outside of a hospital laboratory setting

explanation: Keep it simple! Using everyday language ensures everyone—regardless of their reading level—understands how to protect their health.

question: What important advice should you give a client about her IUD strings?

options.A: Come to the clinic weekly for string trimming
options.B: Pull gently on the strings every morning to check if it's tight
options.C: Cut the strings shorter with scissors if they curl up
options.D: Check for the strings inside the vagina after every monthly period

explanation: Teach clients to do a quick finger check for their strings after their period to make sure the IUD is still sitting snugly in place.

question: Which complication is a top cause of mothers dying during home deliveries?

options.A: Post-term pregnancy
options.B: Mild urinary frequency
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after birth happens fast and can be very dangerous—it's the leading killer of mothers in home birth settings.

question: A community health nurse sets up a free blood sugar screening in the market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Universal prevention

explanation: Great job! Screenings are all about early detection so you can catch health issues early and treat them quickly. That's secondary prevention!

question: By which physical mechanism do oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the placental membrane?

options.A: Pinocytosis
options.B: Facilitated filtration
options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Respiratory gases are small molecules that move passively across the placental membrane following their respective concentration gradients. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h4)

question: A student just lists summaries of ten different articles back-to-back without linking them together. What is the main issue?

options.A: Forgetting to include the personal opinions of the patients
options.B: Using too many references from international nursing journals
options.C: Failing to synthesize and connect the themes across the articles
options.D: Writing the review before collecting any raw clinical data

explanation: A great literature review weaves studies together like a story, showing how they relate instead of reading like a random grocery list.

question: Which artery provides the main blood supply to the abdominal section of the oesophagus?

options.A: Right subclavian artery
options.B: Left gastric artery
options.C: Descending thoracic aorta
options.D: Inferior thyroid artery

explanation: You're learning fast! As the oesophagus drops down into the belly area, it picks up its blood supply mostly from branches of the left gastric artery.

question: How can a Guinea worm infection lead to permanent joint stiffness?

options.A: Systemic fever dissolves the synovial fluid protecting the joint
options.B: Severe local inflammation near a joint causes scar tissue and contractures
options.C: Patients refuse to move their limbs for the rest of their lives
options.D: The worm directly consumes cartilage and bone marrow inside the joint

explanation: Spot on! Bad inflammation and infection near joints can leave behind tight scar tissue that makes movement difficult. You're thinking deeply about patient outcomes!

question: Why isn't the CA-125 blood test used as a general screening tool for healthy women?

options.A: It only detects cancer after it has already spread to the brain
options.B: It requires a painful surgical biopsy before the blood sample is drawn
options.C: It can be elevated by non-cancerous conditions like endometriosis or menstruation
options.D: The cost of the test is too high for public healthcare systems

explanation: You nailed it. Normal things like your period or harmless cysts can also make CA-125 levels rise, leading to false alarms.

question: How does active immunization protect the body against future infections?

options.A: By destroying all existing white blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By transferring ready-made antibodies directly from another person
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce its own antibodies
options.D: By providing instant chemical disinfection on the skin surface

explanation: Active immunity acts like a gym workout for your immune system, teaching it to build its own antibodies and remember germs for later.

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the front soft spot) of a newborn?

options.A: Triangular shape
options.B: Square shape
options.C: Circular shape
options.D: Diamond shape

explanation: The front soft spot (anterior fontanelle) is nicely diamond-shaped. This is a classic midwifery detail that helps you tell it apart from the triangular back soft spot!

question: What is the primary action of a bacteriostatic antibiotic?

options.A: Instantly dissolving the cell wall of all viruses
options.B: Stopping the reproduction and growth of bacteria
options.C: Lowering the patient's fever by acting on the brain
options.D: Stimulating the patient's bone marrow to make platelets

explanation: Bacteriostatic drugs hit the pause button on bacterial multiplication so the body's natural immune system can easily finish clearing them out.

question: When is rabies post-exposure prophylaxis necessary after an animal bite?

options.A: Only if the human victim shows signs of neurological confusion
options.B: If the patient has not received a tetanus shot within the past year
options.C: When the animal is high-risk and unavailable for observation or testing
options.D: Whenever any household pet breaks the skin during playful activity

explanation: If a high-risk animal cannot be tested or watched for signs of rabies, we don't take chances—rabies prophylaxis is started right away.

question: What is the term for weak, lazy uterine contractions that fail to open the cervix?

options.A: Occiput posterior
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Uterine inertia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

explanation: Spot on! 'Inertia' means lack of movement or energy. The uterus is simply too tired or weak to push the process along.

question: Which of the following is evaluated when assessing the sensory system during a neurological exam?

options.A: Light touch and pain perception
options.B: Muscle bulk and involuntary twitching
options.C: Deep tendon reflex hammer response
options.D: Level of orientation to time and place

explanation: Sensory evaluations focus on how well the patient perceives external stimuli like touch, pain, and vibration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which of these terms describes multicellular parasitic worms?

options.A: Bacteria
options.B: Helminths
options.C: Ectoparasites
options.D: Protozoa

explanation: Spot on! Helminths are multicellular worms (like tapeworms and roundworms). Protozoa are tiny and single-celled, while ectoparasites hang out on the outside of the skin.

question: What is the very first thing you check when a patient arrives with an acute sting?

options.A: Applying a cold ice pack to reduce swelling
options.B: Assessing airway, breathing, and circulation
options.C: Inquiring about past medical history
options.D: Cleaning the wound with soap and water

explanation: Always ABCs first! Checking airway, breathing, and circulation helps you catch severe allergic reactions or shock before they get out of hand.

question: Which preventive measure is especially recommended to protect older adults from bacterial pneumonia?

options.A: Taking daily antibiotics just in case
options.B: Staying indoors all the time
options.C: Pneumococcal vaccination
options.D: Using a home air humidifier

explanation: Vaccines are a powerful shield! The pneumococcal vaccine helps older adults and high-risk patients fight off dangerous strains of pneumonia.

question: What is the key difference between inherited and acquired bleeding disorders?

options.A: Acquired disorders are present from birth.
options.B: Inherited disorders are passed down through genetics.
options.C: Inherited disorders develop later in life from poor diet.
options.D: Acquired disorders never involve platelet abnormalities.

explanation: Spot on! Inherited conditions are handed down through family genes from birth, while acquired disorders pop up later in life due to things like illness, diet, or medications.

question: Why is routine clamping of a chest tube strongly discouraged when moving a patient?

options.A: It permanently ruins the plastic collection chambers of the unit
options.B: It increases the risk of severe infection at the insertion site
options.C: It can quickly cause a life-threatening tension pneumothorax
options.D: It causes the sterile water in the seal chamber to evaporate

explanation: Clamping traps air and fluid with nowhere to go. This can cause the lung to collapse rapidly, so avoid clamping unless ordered for specific tests!

question: During a virtual visit, what is one of the main things a tele-nurse does?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations
options.B: Triage and symptom assessment
options.C: Manufacturing medical devices
options.D: Operating hospital financial accounts

explanation: Tele-nurses spend a lot of time listening to patient complaints, checking symptoms, and figuring out how urgently they need care.

question: How does the body get rid of extra fluid from the skin and tissues right after birth?

options.A: Through rapid shedding of the top layer of skin cells
options.B: By reabsorbing all fluid directly back into the digestive tract
options.C: Through heavy postpartum sweating and increased urination
options.D: By storing extra fluid permanently in the muscle tissue

explanation: Sweating buckets and frequent bathroom trips are your body's clever ways of clearing out all that extra pregnancy fluid!

question: When plotting your findings on the partograph, which symbol do you use to mark cervical dilation?

options.A: An 'X'
options.B: A triangle
options.C: A square
options.D: A star

explanation: You'll use an 'X' for cervical dilation, and a circle ('O') to track how far down the baby's head is descending. You've got this!

question: How can a nurse best support an elderly patient with low literacy who takes multiple medications?

options.A: By stopping all medications until literacy classes are completed
options.B: By using pictorial charts and involving a reliable family caregiver
options.C: By writing complex medical terms down on a small paper slip
options.D: By telling the patient to memorize the pill colors and shapes

explanation: Visual aids like pictures and symbols overcome literacy barriers, while family involvement provides vital daily supervision and support. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h5)

question: What happens to a patient's body weight when their daily calorie intake matches what they burn?

options.A: Body weight increases rapidly
options.B: Body weight remains stable
options.C: Body weight decreases steadily
options.D: Metabolic rate stops functioning

explanation: When energy in equals energy out, your weight stays steady. Perfect balance!

question: What is a key nursing duty right before a patient takes a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Confirming that the patient actually followed the fasting rules
options.B: Giving the patient a small snack to boost energy
options.C: Checking their urine output with a dipstick
options.D: Giving a quick dose of insulin just in case

explanation: Always double-check! Asking 'When was your last meal or drink?' ensures you don't send inaccurate lab samples to the path lab.

question: What is a major disadvantage of bilateral tubal ligation compared to barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: It requires daily motivation and adherence from the client.
options.B: It immediately causes early menopause and hot flashes.
options.C: It has a very high failure rate within the first year.
options.D: It offers no protection against sexually transmitted infections.

explanation: While highly effective at preventing pregnancy, tubal ligation does not shield against sexually transmitted infections, unlike barrier methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: Why do women pregnant with multiples need extra iron and folic acid supplements?

options.A: To suppress the natural production of amniotic fluid
options.B: To support the massive expansion of blood volume and fetal growth
options.C: To help tighten the pelvic floor muscles before labor
options.D: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Spot on! Two (or more) babies mean the mum needs way more blood and nutrients to support everyone. Extra supplements help keep deficiency anemia far away.

question: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is responsible for a severe, rapid anaphylactic allergic response?

options.A: Type II
options.B: Type I
options.C: Type IV
options.D: Type III

explanation: Type I reactions are immediate, IgE-mediated responses that can quickly escalate to life-threatening anaphylaxis. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is a main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To provide extra funding for international medical research
options.B: To allocate limited healthcare resources where they are needed most
options.C: To replace the need for individual patient physical examinations
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in private hospitals

explanation: Resources are always limited, so finding the highest priority problems ensures supplies and personnel go where they will do the most good. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why is relying on informal personal shortcuts instead of established hospital policy dangerous?

options.A: It forces the hospital to buy expensive new computer systems
options.B: It creates inconsistency and increases the risk of medical errors
options.C: It automatically increases the nurse's monthly salary
options.D: It saves too much time and makes nursing look too easy

explanation: Informal shortcuts bypass vital safety checks, leading to unpredictable care quality and a higher chance of making a mistake.

question: A male patient with severe chest pain waited three days to visit the clinic because he felt he had to 'be strong' for his family. Which concept best explains this delay?

options.A: An innate genetic flaw in male chromosome pairing
options.B: Socially constructed gender roles influencing health-seeking behavior
options.C: A standard physiological reaction to low blood pressure
options.D: An intersex hormonal imbalance affecting pain receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Traditional masculine expectations to be stoic can sadly stop men from seeking quick medical attention.

question: Which blood test is commonly checked to assess a patient's nutrition before surgery?

options.A: Serum albumin
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood glucose
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: You got it! Serum albumin is a classic protein marker we use to check a surgical patient's nutritional reserves.

question: How does setting small, realistic goals during follow-up visits help the patient?

options.A: It ensures the nurse does not have to do any paperwork
options.B: It replaces the need for any professional medical treatment
options.C: It builds their confidence and encourages active participation in recovery
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will never feel stressed again

explanation: Achievable goals empower patients, making them feel capable and involved in managing their own health. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: What visual characteristic does urine often have in a patient with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: Dark red and bloody
options.B: Frothy or foamy appearance
options.C: Thick and milky white
options.D: Bright neon green color

explanation: The large amount of protein spilling into the urine changes its surface tension, creating a noticeable frothy or foamy look when the patient voids. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which touch receptor is responsible for feeling deep pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Meissner corpuscles
options.C: Merkel discs
options.D: Ruffini endings

explanation: You nailed it! Pacinian corpuscles are large, deep receptors built specifically to catch rapid vibrations and heavy pressure.

question: What do we call the joint right at the front where the pubic bones meet?

options.A: Pubic symphysis
options.B: Acetabulum
options.C: Lumbosacral joint
options.D: Sacroiliac joint

explanation: Great job! The pubic symphysis is simply the cartilaginous joint joining the right and left pubic bones right at the front midline.

question: When an adverse event happens, what is the main goal of using 'systems thinking'?

options.A: Focusing entirely on disciplining the nurse who made the final error
options.B: Reducing the number of nursing staff on duty during night shifts
options.C: Moving away from blaming individuals toward fixing workflow processes
options.D: Assuming that technology can completely eliminate all human mistakes

explanation: Systems thinking stops the blame game. Instead of pointing fingers at a colleague, it looks at the environment and structural issues that allowed the error to happen in the first place.

question: A patient has been vomiting nonstop for three days. Which blood lab imbalance should the nurse expect?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Metabolic acidosis

explanation: Brilliant! Throwing up all that stomach acid (hydrochloric acid) leaves the body with extra bicarbonate, pushing the blood into metabolic alkalosis. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: Why do oral medications have to pass through the liver before reaching the rest of the body?

options.A: The liver is the primary site where red blood cells absorb the drug
options.B: Stomach acid forces the drug directly into the bile ducts
options.C: Bile salts are required to activate every type of oral pill
options.D: Hepatic first-pass metabolism alters or breaks down part of the drug

explanation: This is known as the 'first-pass effect'! Blood from your gut goes straight to the liver via the portal vein, where liver enzymes get the first chance to process or break down a portion of the drug.

question: Which of these is NOT a way that food preservation methods work?

options.A: By mutating microbial DNA into beneficial human cells
options.B: By removing moisture needed for bacteria to multiply
options.C: By altering temperatures to halt microbial growth
options.D: By using physical or chemical barriers to stop contamination

explanation: Spot on! Preservation stops microbes through drying, cooling, or chemicals—it definitely doesn't turn germs into human cells!

question: Which tool do event managers commonly use to watch crowd movement and density in real time?

options.A: Post-event questionnaires
options.B: Weekly weather forecasts
options.C: Closed-circuit television cameras
options.D: Paper registration logs

explanation: CCTV camera feeds give security and medical teams 'eyes everywhere' so they can spot crowd build-ups instantly.

question: Which chemical messenger is blocked by anticholinergic anti-spasmodics to stop cramps?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the chemical messenger that tells your gut muscles to squeeze. Anticholinergics step in to block it, helping the muscles finally relax.

question: What is the best reaction when a community nurse discovers a patient is using traditional herbal remedies alongside prescribed drugs?

options.A: Refuse to treat the patient until they sign an apology
options.B: Yell at the patient immediately and throw the herbs away
options.C: Report the patient to local security agencies at once
options.D: Discuss the herbs calmly to check for any dangerous drug interactions

explanation: A non-judgmental approach helps patients feel safe to share their habits, allowing the nurse to protect them from harmful drug-herb interactions. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: A nurse sets up a desk in the village square to check blood sugar levels for healthy adults. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Quaternary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: You nailed it! Screening tests catch health issues early before big symptoms show up, which is what secondary prevention is all about.

question: What are the three main behaviors checked when scoring the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)?

options.A: Reflexes, muscle tone, and pupil size
options.B: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure
options.C: Sensory touch, pain, and temperature
options.D: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response

explanation: You've got this! The GCS looks at these three simple reactions to quickly check how well the brain is functioning.

question: What is the main purpose of defining a 'case' during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: To ensure everyone uses the exact same criteria to count infected people
options.B: To find out which nurse made a charting mistake
options.C: To prove that the hospital is free of bacteria
options.D: To decide which patients must pay for their treatment

explanation: A clear case definition ensures accurate data collection without overcounting or undercounting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is a major risk when international donors fund specific health programs?

options.A: They may ignore broader, foundational healthcare needs
options.B: They always cause the complete closure of local hospitals
options.C: They force nurses to stop practicing traditional methods
options.D: They remove all need for government budgeting

explanation: Donor funding often comes with strict conditions targeting single diseases, which can distract from overall health system strengthening. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a BCC program?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.B: Evaluation happens before the project starts, and monitoring never happens
options.C: There is no difference; both words mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation measures final impact

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your progress while running the race, and evaluation as looking at your overall performance and medals when the race is finished. You've got this distinction down!

question: Why is taking a nighttime dose of a cystine-binding medication so important?

options.A: Cystine excretion often peaks at night during periods of sleep and dehydration
options.B: Kidney blood flow drops to zero during deep sleep, requiring higher drug levels
options.C: Bedtime dosing completely eliminates the need for daytime water intake
options.D: The liver metabolizes the medication much faster during daylight hours

explanation: At night, we sleep without drinking water, making our urine concentrated. A bedtime dose protects the kidneys during those vulnerable overnight hours!

question: Who is protected when a nurse properly uses isolation precautions?

options.A: Only the doctors working in the ward
options.B: Only the patient who is currently sick
options.C: Patients, healthcare workers, and visitors
options.D: Hospital management and administrators

explanation: Infection control keeps everyone in the hospital safe and sound—patients, your colleagues, and loved ones who come to visit!

question: A patient says her periods always arrive every 28 days, last 5 days, and have a moderate flow. What is your best initial nursing action?

options.A: Document this as a normal finding in her chart
options.B: Instruct her to start taking oral contraceptives
options.C: Order emergency hormone blood tests
options.D: Refer her immediately to a gynecological surgeon

explanation: A classic 28-day cycle with moderate flow is textbook normal! No interventions or emergency tests are needed—just a clean, accurate chart entry.

question: A young man comes to the clinic with sudden, severe pain in one side of his scrotum, and the testicle appears unusually high. What is the most likely issue?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Chronic epididymitis
options.C: Testicular torsion
options.D: Hydrocele formation

explanation: Sudden, severe scrotal pain with a high-riding testicle is the classic red flag for testicular torsion. Always watch out for this in clinical practice!

question: Which common insect breeds like crazy in stagnant floodwaters after heavy rains or a disaster?

options.A: Earthworms
options.B: Mosquitoes
options.C: Butterflies
options.D: Honeybees

explanation: Still floodwaters are breeding paradises for mosquitoes, driving up malaria risks. Netting and draining standing water are key nursing interventions!

question: Why do hospitals nowadays rarely give whole blood to patients?

options.A: Whole blood carries no oxygen-carrying capacity
options.B: Patients usually only need specific blood components
options.C: Whole blood spoils within two hours of collection
options.D: Processing whole blood is too expensive for hospitals

explanation: Great job thinking like a clinician! Blood is separated into parts so patients get precisely what they lack—like just red cells or platelets—rather than getting components they don't need.

question: What is the main goal of using a partograph during active labour?

options.A: To track labour progress and detect deviations early
options.B: To document the baby's growth during antenatal clinics
options.C: To measure the mother's daily nutritional intake
options.D: To calculate the exact date of conception

explanation: You've got it! The partograph gives us a clear picture of how labour is going so we can catch any problems before they become emergencies.

question: Six hours after a circumcision, you notice steady, active bleeding from the wound edge. What is your FIRST nursing action?

options.A: Soak the entire genital area in warm soapy bath water
options.B: Apply direct, firm pressure to the bleeding site with sterile gauze
options.C: Administer a stat dose of intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.D: Wait patiently to see if the bleeding stops on its own within an hour

explanation: Always start with direct pressure using sterile gauze to control bleeding while you call for the doctor to assist.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard infection control practice in the home?

options.A: Cleaning equipment according to manufacturer guidelines
options.B: Disposing of used needles in a puncture-proof container
options.C: Keeping clean medical supplies separate from household waste
options.D: Washing hands only once at the beginning of the nursing shift

explanation: Spot on! Hand hygiene must be done frequently before and after patient contact, not just once when you walk through the door. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of a hierarchical communication barrier?

options.A: A junior nurse being too intimidated to report a abnormal sign to a senior doctor
options.B: A nurse misunderstanding a medical term written in a foreign language
options.C: A noisy infusion pump beeping loudly in a crowded intensive care unit
options.D: A tired staff member forgetting to read the morning shift handover notes

explanation: Fear of authority and strict power gaps create hierarchical barriers that prevent vital patient safety information from traveling upward. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why is just handing out a new safety checklist usually not enough to change hospital practice?

options.A: Habits require ongoing reinforcement and audit to stick
options.B: Checklists are illegal in most healthcare settings
options.C: Doctors refuse to let nurses use checklists
options.D: Paper checklists take too much time to complete

explanation: Just giving out a new tool won't change daily habits unless there is proper follow-up, training, and regular performance checks.

question: What does a grassroots approach to community health rely on most?

options.A: Complete reliance on imported foods for malnourished children
options.B: Strict enforcement of police patrols around local markets
options.C: Direct funding and management by foreign governments only
options.D: Active involvement and ownership by local community members

explanation: Grassroots programs succeed by empowering local residents to lead and sustain health initiatives within their own homes and villages.

question: Which specific questionnaire is widely used to screen mothers for postpartum depression?

options.A: Apgar scoring system
options.B: Bishop cervical score
options.C: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: Spot on! The Edinburgh scale is a short, trusted questionnaire designed to help nurses catch signs of depression in new mothers early.

question: How does an overly competitive and hostile classroom climate affect students?

options.A: It speeds up the mastery of human anatomy
options.B: It breeds stress and fear of asking questions
options.C: It removes all forms of academic anxiety
options.D: It encourages open sharing of clinical techniques

explanation: Hostile environments make students terrified of looking foolish, which stops them from asking the vital questions they need to learn.

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital during family planning sessions?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek needed care safely
options.B: It guarantees that the government will fund the clinic supplies
options.C: It prevents hospital administrators from auditing patient records
options.D: It stops family members from asking about the client's health

explanation: Clients need assurance that their private reproductive health details will not be shared openly in the community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: Why do doctors often combine NK1 blockers and steroids with 5-HT3 drugs for patients on strong chemotherapy?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for intravenous fluid replacement
options.B: They prevent hair loss caused by aggressive cytotoxic medications
options.C: They neutralize the chemotherapy drugs before they damage the stomach
options.D: They target multiple distinct pathways to prevent both acute and delayed nausea

explanation: You nailed it! Hitting different receptors at the same time gives the best defense against tough, multi-day chemotherapy nausea. Teamwork in pharmacology!

question: What does the principle of autonomy mean in family planning?

options.A: Clinics must provide free medications to every community member
options.B: Husbands must approve all medical treatments before they begin
options.C: Clients have the right to make their own choices without coercion
options.D: Nurses must choose the safest contraceptive for young clients

explanation: Autonomy protects the client's right to self-determination in their personal reproductive healthcare decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: A mother brings her healthy six-month-old baby to the clinic. What services should she get today?

options.A: Dental extraction and eye surgery
options.B: Emergency malaria treatment and blood transfusion
options.C: Surgical screening and X-ray imaging
options.D: Growth check, scheduled vaccines, and weaning advice

explanation: Well done! A healthy six-month-old needs a quick weight check, their due immunizations, and a friendly chat about starting solid foods (weaning).

question: When public health experts calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio, what is the standard denominator used?

options.A: Per 10,000 total women
options.B: Per 100,000 live births
options.C: Per 1,000 live births
options.D: Per 1,000 pregnant women

explanation: Great to know for exams and clinical practice: maternal mortality ratio is always expressed per 100,000 live births. You're doing brilliantly!

question: A patient with high blood pressure loves strongly salted local seasonings. What is the most practical nursing approach?

options.A: Prescribe an expensive imported meal plan from another continent
options.B: Suggest reducing the salt gradually and using local aromatic herbs for flavor
options.C: Ignore their diet since salt intake has no effect on blood pressure
options.D: Tell the patient they must never taste local soup again for the rest of their life

explanation: Offering realistic tweaks like local herbs for flavor respects their food preferences while protecting their heart health. You've got this!

question: Why is drying the newborn baby immediately after birth a critical nursing action?

options.A: To stimulate the baby to learn how to walk
options.B: To remove the vernix completely so the skin breathes
options.C: To check for hidden birthmarks and bruises
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

explanation: Wet skin combined with room air causes rapid evaporation and heat loss, which can lead to dangerous cold stress in newborns. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h3)

question: How does evaluation differ from routine monitoring in health programmes?

options.A: Evaluation is only performed before the project begins
options.B: Monitoring is done exclusively by government ministers
options.C: Evaluation measures long-term outcomes and overall impact
options.D: Monitoring focuses strictly on community financial budgets

explanation: You've got this! Monitoring tracks daily work, while evaluation looks at the big picture to see if the overall health goals were finally met.

question: During which phase of the nursing process does the nurse actually perform interventions like wound care or medication administration?

options.A: Implementation
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Evaluation
options.D: Planning

explanation: Implementation is the action phase where the nurse carries out the planned care interventions. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of adding social inclusion into nursing care plans?

options.A: To ensure that all hospital beds are filled by patients from identical backgrounds
options.B: To eliminate the need for physicians to write formal medical prescriptions
options.C: To empower vulnerable patients and reduce health disparities caused by social inequality
options.D: To force patients to change their cultural and religious beliefs before discharge

explanation: Social inclusion in nursing is all about making sure everyone gets fair, respectful care by tackling the root causes of discrimination and helping patients speak for themselves.

question: Why must minor tranquilizers be reduced slowly (tapered) instead of stopping them all at once?

options.A: To ensure the prescription lasts until the next clinic visit
options.B: To allow the liver time to regenerate damaged cells
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing immediate weight gain
options.D: To prevent dangerous withdrawal symptoms like seizures

explanation: Stopping suddenly after the body has gotten used to the drug can cause severe rebound anxiety or even seizures. Safety first!

question: Why is simply giving people health information (one-way sharing) often not enough on its own?

options.A: It automatically causes confusion among patients
options.B: It requires too many expensive laboratory tests
options.C: It fails to address deep-seated social norms and personal habits
options.D: It can only be delivered by senior medical doctors

explanation: You got it! Just telling people what to do isn't enough; changing human habits and cultural routines takes real engagement and ongoing support.

question: What is the very first thing you should do right after giving an injection?

options.A: Break the needle off the syringe barrel before throwing it in the trash
options.B: Activate the safety device and drop the syringe into a sharps container
options.C: Recap the needle firmly using both hands to protect housekeeping staff
options.D: Place the exposed needle on the bedside tray until documentation is done

explanation: Safety first! Never recap needles with two hands. Pop the safety shield on and drop the whole syringe straight into the sharps box to avoid nasty needle-stick injuries.

question: Which receptors does norepinephrine target to keep the penis in a flaccid state?

options.A: Beta-2 adrenergic receptors
options.B: Nicotinic cholinergic receptors
options.C: Alpha-1 adrenergic receptors
options.D: Muscarinic cholinergic receptors

explanation: Keep it up! Norepinephrine binds to alpha-1 receptors on the smooth muscles, making them contract and keep blood flow low.

question: What is the official paper form that Nigerian health workers use to report adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Blue Card Sheet
options.B: Yellow Form
options.C: Red Discharge Tag
options.D: Green Admission Book

explanation: Whenever you spot a nasty drug reaction in practice, grab the NAFDAC Yellow Form and report it!

question: What is the main chemical powder used to make a Plaster of Paris cast?

options.A: Calcium carbonate flakes
options.B: Magnesium sulfate paste
options.C: Calcium sulfate hemihydrate
options.D: Sodium chloride crystals

explanation: Dry Plaster of Paris is made of calcium sulfate hemihydrate. When you mix it with water, it changes into a dihydrate form and hardens!

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard duty for a clinical nurse regarding waste management?

options.A: Educating patients on safe disposal of personal medical items
options.B: Designing and building new municipal waste landfills
options.C: Reporting damaged or overfilled sharp containers
options.D: Segregating items into appropriate colored bins

explanation: Correct! Building landfills is the job of civil and environmental engineers, not clinical nurses. You're doing great!

question: What does a very large volume of distribution tell us about a drug?

options.A: The kidneys are getting rid of the drug too fast
options.B: The patient's liver is breaking down the medicine rapidly
options.C: The drug has moved heavily out of the blood and into body tissues
options.D: The drug is trapped strictly inside the blood vessels

explanation: A high volume of distribution means the drug loves hiding out in fat or muscle and leaves very little of itself floating behind in the blood.

question: Which of these is a dangerous and incorrect practice with disposable medical gloves?

options.A: Cleaning your hands before putting them on
options.B: Choosing nitrile instead of latex
options.C: Washing and reusing them between patients
options.D: Changing them after every single patient

explanation: Disposable gloves are strictly single-use! Washing them ruins their protective barrier and spreads germs around the ward.

question: Why is proper lighting and full exposure of the joint necessary during a musculoskeletal assessment?

options.A: To make it easier for the doctor to read the laboratory results
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling cold in the examination room
options.C: To ensure the patient's blood pressure remains stable throughout the test
options.D: To accurately observe subtle skin changes, swelling, and muscle symmetry

explanation: Good light and clear visibility let the nurse spot minor differences in size, shape, or color between limbs. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why would a doctor order a plain spine X-ray for a patient who just fell?

options.A: To see if the spinal cord is bruised or swollen
options.B: To look for hidden bleeding inside the brain
options.C: To measure how fast nerves carry signals
options.D: To check bone alignment and rule out broken bones

explanation: Spine X-rays give a quick view of bone structure to make sure there are no fractures after a fall.

question: Which simple tool does a healthcare provider use to actually see a cervical polyp?

options.A: Stethoscope
options.B: Otoscope
options.C: Speculum
options.D: Sphygmomanometer

explanation: A speculum gently opens the vaginal canal so the doctor can get a clear, direct look at the cervix.

question: What is closed-loop communication in a clinical setting?

options.A: Talking only through written memos left in a locked box
options.B: The receiver repeats the instruction back to confirm understanding
options.C: Using encrypted messaging apps for all doctor handovers
options.D: Restricting conversations to the nurse's station only

explanation: Closed-loop communication stops dangerous mistakes by ensuring the sender hears the exact message echoed back accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h4)

question: What often causes the biggest hurdles for people with physical disabilities in daily life?

options.A: Inaccessible physical environments and negative social attitudes
options.B: A lack of interest in attending family social gatherings
options.C: The mandatory use of modern assistive walking frames
options.D: Excessive consumption of prescribed rehabilitation vitamins

explanation: Often, bad societal attitudes and buildings without ramps or lifts cause more barriers than the physical condition itself. We must be change agents!

question: What does the term socioeconomic status primarily include?

options.A: Exercise habits and sleep patterns
options.B: Genetics, height, and blood type
options.C: Income, education, and occupation
options.D: Age, gender, and family size

explanation: Socioeconomic status measures a person's standing in society using factors like how much they earn, the job they do, and their level of education. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h1)

question: Why do fistula patients often develop painful sores on their inner thighs?

options.A: Continuous exposure of the skin to the irritating effects of urine
options.B: A rare allergic reaction to hospital bedsheets and blankets
options.C: Fungal skin infections spread from poor personal hygiene
options.D: Pressure sores caused by sitting in a wheelchair for too long

explanation: Exactly! Constant dampness breaks down the skin barrier, leading to painful irritation and excoriation around the thighs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why is spotting delivery complications early at a primary health centre so crucial?

options.A: It ensures the family will pay the delivery fees on time
options.B: It guarantees the baby will be born without any health issues
options.C: It allows the nurse to intervene or arrange transfer before full collapse happens
options.D: It completely stops the normal labor process from continuing

explanation: Catching warning signs early gives you precious time to start emergency steps and move the mother safely before things get out of hand.

question: Why is it a bad idea to sort mixed waste later in the utility room?

options.A: It greatly increases the risk of accidental needlestick injuries.
options.B: It causes color-coded bags to fade under fluorescent lights.
options.C: It makes the municipal waste collectors charge extra fees.
options.D: It takes too much time away from cleaning patient rooms.

explanation: Never rummage through bags of unsorted waste! You might accidentally poke yourself on a hidden needle or touch dangerous fluids.

question: Which antenatal care service is most crucial for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Intensive nutritional counseling and iron supplementation
options.B: Mandatory enrollment in adult literacy classes
options.C: Immediate scheduling of elective tubal ligation
options.D: Restriction of physical activity throughout all trimesters

explanation: Because teen moms are still growing and easily get anemic, good nutrition guidance and iron supplements are absolute top priorities.

question: What is the main job of normal lymphocytes in our body?

options.A: Fighting off infections and foreign invaders
options.B: Producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Clotting blood to prevent bleeding
options.D: Carrying oxygen to body tissues

explanation: Think of lymphocytes as part of your body's security team! They are white blood cells that protect you against bacteria, viruses, and other germs.

question: What is the ultimate goal of Universal Health Coverage (UHC)?

options.A: Ensuring everyone gets needed health services without financial hardship
options.B: Making all hospitals in the country completely free and private
options.C: Eliminating the need for nurses and doctors in rural areas
options.D: Requiring every citizen to travel abroad for complex surgeries

explanation: UHC simply means everyone can walk into a hospital, get quality treatment, and not go broke doing it.

question: When a nurse steps up to protect a patient's rights and safety, what role are they playing?

options.A: Advocate
options.B: Surgical operator
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Hospital accountant

explanation: You got it! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients' rights, safety, and best interests when they are most vulnerable. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: A hospital wants to check if their new nurse-led clinic actually lowered stroke rates over the past 5 years. What type of activity is this?

options.A: Evaluation, because it looks at long-term outcomes and overall impact
options.B: Monitoring, because it tracks daily blood pressure checks
options.C: Budgeting, because it calculates the cost of stethoscopes
options.D: Auditing, because it checks if nurses sign patient charts

explanation: Looking back over several years to see if health truly improved is a big-picture evaluation, not just daily monitoring.

question: Why is recording baseline vital signs and functional ability on the initial assessment sheet important?

options.A: It proves to the family that the nurse arrived on time
options.B: It provides a starting point to measure future clinical progress or decline
options.C: It allows the nurse to discharge the client immediately on day one
options.D: It satisfies administrative paperwork without affecting daily nursing care

explanation: Baseline data gives the nurse a clear point of comparison to see if treatments are working or if the client's health is worsening. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: If nurses on a ward keep leaving used needles uncapped on trays, what is the best way to fix this habit?

options.A: Issue written warning letters to every single nurse working in the ward
options.B: Ban all injections in the facility until staff members remember the rules
options.C: Conduct training sessions and place safety boxes closer to the point of use
options.D: Wait for the next annual hospital inspection to report the problem

explanation: Making safety gear easy to reach and providing supportive training works much better than punishment for changing clinical habits.

question: Which type of infection control precautions must you practice with every single patient you care for?

options.A: Airborne precautions
options.B: Droplet precautions
options.C: Contact precautions
options.D: Standard precautions

explanation: Awesome! Standard precautions are our everyday baseline protection for every patient, no matter their diagnosis.

question: Why do nurses worry so much about secondary complications after a bone fracture?

options.A: They only affect the skin layers surrounding the bone injury.
options.B: They can sometimes become more dangerous than the original break.
options.C: They always require immediate amputation of the affected limb.
options.D: They prevent the patient from ever walking without crutches.

explanation: While a broken bone hurts badly, issues that happen afterwards—like severe infections or blood clots—can actually threaten a patient's life or limb. Spotting them early is a key part of your nursing care!

question: Why is psychological rehab just as vital as physical detox when treating substance dependence?

options.A: It replaces the need for any nursing observation or vital sign monitoring
options.B: It ensures the patient never experiences physical withdrawal symptoms again
options.C: It addresses underlying triggers and teaches healthy coping skills to prevent relapse
options.D: It is the only way to restore normal kidney and liver function after drug use

explanation: Brilliant! Detox cleans out the body, but rehab tackles the emotional and behavioral roots of addiction so the patient can learn new ways to cope without drugs.

question: Which type of thread is used for outer skin stitches and needs to be taken out after a few days?

options.A: Absorbable suture
options.B: Non-absorbable suture
options.C: Catgut suture
options.D: Biodegradable thread

explanation: Non-absorbable materials like nylon give strong outer support while the skin heals, and we remove them during a follow-up visit. Easypz!

question: What is a primary purpose of follow-up bereavement services provided by a hospice team?

options.A: To help surviving family members navigate their grief
options.B: To collect remaining financial payments for the facility
options.C: To conduct research on terminal disease progression
options.D: To evaluate the medical skills of the nursing staff

explanation: Support groups and counseling help families cope with the emotional and physical challenges of the grieving process. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h8)

question: Why is a sputum culture ordered when a client has a persistent productive cough?

options.A: To identify the specific microorganism causing an infection
options.B: To measure the total daily volume of mucus production
options.C: To check if the client has smoked cigarettes recently
options.D: To evaluate how well the lungs exchange gases

explanation: Culturing mucus allows the laboratory to grow the infectious agent and determine which antibiotic will treat it best. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred during a dietary interview?

options.A: They encourage the patient to share detailed information
options.B: They guarantee the patient will follow the diet plan
options.C: They take less time to complete than closed questions
options.D: They prevent the patient from asking questions back

explanation: Open-ended questions require more than a simple 'yes' or 'no' answer, opening up a meaningful conversation. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h4)

question: What fluid do continuous glucose monitors sample to check a patient's sugar levels?

options.A: Epidermal sweat
options.B: Interstitial fluid
options.C: Capillary whole blood
options.D: Venous plasma

explanation: The tiny sensor sits right under the skin, swimming in the fluid surrounding your cells (interstitial fluid) to estimate blood sugar.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to assess a patient's spiritual needs even if they do not share the same religious beliefs?

options.A: Because spiritual distress can cause deep emotional and physical suffering
options.B: To satisfy mandatory legal requirements for hospital discharge
options.C: Because chaplains are not allowed to speak with patients alone
options.D: To convert the patient to the nurse's personal faith

explanation: Spiritual health directly impacts overall well-being and comfort, making assessment crucial for comprehensive palliative nursing care regardless of personal beliefs. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h4)

question: Which statement is true about Type IV FGM?

options.A: It still poses serious risks of bleeding, pain, and infection
options.B: It is always performed by licensed medical doctors
options.C: It is universally recognized as a form of childbirth preparation
options.D: It carries no risk of infection because it is minor

explanation: Correct! Even though Type IV uses different methods like piercing or scraping, any non-medical cutting of genital tissue carries high risks.

question: Why are nurses strongly advised NOT to recap used needles?

options.A: It violates hospital rules regarding plastic waste recycling
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of accidental needle stick injuries
options.C: It damages the sharp tip making it useless for the next patient
options.D: It wastes valuable nursing time during busy medication rounds

explanation: Trying to guide a tiny cap back onto a used needle is one of the quickest ways to accidentally poke yourself. Drop it straight into the safety box instead!

question: What is one of the most common ways nurses accidentally get needle-stick injuries on duty?

options.A: Transporting bins during morning shift changes
options.B: Recapping used injection needles
options.C: Using plastic syringes instead of glass
options.D: Emptying safety boxes when they are full

explanation: Spot on. Trying to guide a cap back onto a used needle puts your fingers right in the line of fire. Best practice? Never recap needles!

question: Why is it important to watch the client's face during passive exercises?

options.A: To check if they are watching the television
options.B: To spot hidden pain or distress when they cannot speak well
options.C: To check how fast their hair is growing
options.D: To see if they need spectacles to read

explanation: Wonderful! Many patients can't tell you when it hurts, so a quick wince or frown on their face tells you everything you need to know.

question: What is an important safety action when a patient wants to use herbal supplements in the hospital?

options.A: Encourage the patient to double their dosage for faster healing
options.B: Confiscate all herbal products immediately because they are dangerous
options.C: Ignore what the patient takes as long as they swallow their pills
options.D: Screen the supplements for potential interactions with prescribed medications

explanation: Spot on! Herbal products can react strongly with conventional drugs, so as nurses, we always check for safety interactions first.

question: What is a common long-term problem after severe injury and healing of the voice box (larynx)?

options.A: Loss of the sense of smell and taste
options.B: Spontaneous closure of the food pipe
options.C: Airway narrowing (stenosis) from scar tissue
options.D: Permanent widening of the windpipe
